encounter: E0171 TRAINER_NORMAN_1 (Petalburg Gym leader, Balance Badge, cap 42, Medium) - attempt 2 rebuild
availability_audit: Cap-42 window covers Route 111 / Ashen Woods / Petalburg Gym (battle_index campaign_order 151-171), everything after the Heat Badge. Every member's pool-42.json gate is 36 or lower, so each source map is entered strictly before Petalburg Gym in book chapter order: Litten line (Heat Badge window, gate 36), Thwackey/Rillaboom (gate 36), Scyther+Metal Coat (gate 30) with Scizorite stone-window 30, Haunter+Linking Cord (gate 30), Sneasel (gate 14), New Mauville with Wattson's Basement Key (gate 30). No cap-42-gated desert species used, no legendaries. Iron Hands is a Paradox species in a window far above 24, which the brief permits.
plan: Attempt 1 lost to the second half of the fight: Mega Alakazam's forced Trace copied Slaking's Truant the instant Neutralizing Gas dropped and loafed itself to death, and Life Orb Meloetta's Psychic under a Terrain-Extender Psychic Terrain (1.3x, and Expanding Force turned into a spread move) erased Togekiss and Iron Hands. Attempt 2 attacks the terrain instead of the Pokemon: Rillaboom's Grassy Surge overwrites Psychic Terrain, which removes Expanding Force's spread mode and Meloetta's 1.3x at once, halves Slaking's High Horsepower, heals my side every turn and gives my priority back (Psychic Terrain had been blanking Fake Out, Ice Shard and Bullet Punch against grounded targets). Around it: Incineroar and Weavile are Dark bodies immune to Psychic, Mega Scizor resists Psychic and Normal and answers Galarian Weezing with Steel, Gengar is the hard Slaking wall once the Gas is gone (Ghost blanks Double-Edge and Hammer Arm, Levitate blanks High Horsepower, only Ice Punch touches it), and Iron Hands' Heavy Slam is the opening 2x on Weezing while Drain Punch is 2x on every Normal-type Norman owns. Gengar's Taunt is aimed at Indeedee, whose whole kit (Follow Me, Helping Hand, Protect) is status moves.
